subject: Zephyrus: On‑Prem / VPC Capability Survey — Redwood Private details
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@zephyrus.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@zephyrus.com, J. Park <j.park@zephyrus.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Mar 2028 16:42:00 -0400
Subject: RFP: On‑Prem Capability Survey — Zephyrus

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the throughput numbers. Procurement and InfoSec asked us to collect a vendor capability questionnaire before we proceed to contracting and a short PoC. Attached is the survey PDF; key asks include air‑gap installability, KMS/HSM integration, evidence of SBOM and patch cadence, rollback/upgrade playbooks, and that we can run within our SOC‑validated VPC.

Can you confirm you’ll provide an answered survey + supporting artifacts (SBOM, install plan, example network diagram) by EOD Friday 31 Mar? Also flag any "no" answers or items that require an exception.

We may have a short call after your submission (30–45m) to go through clarifications.

Alex
Alex Kim
Sr. Security Architect | Zephyrus Systems
Alex.Kim@zephyrus.com

Attachment: Zephyrus_Capability_Survey_20280324.pdf (PDF, 24 pages)
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@zephyrus.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Mar 2028 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: On‑Prem Capability Survey — Zephyrus

Hi Alex —

Appreciate the clear asks and the timeline. We’ll own the questionnaire and gather artifacts. Marissa (security lead for Private) will prepare the SBOM and install plan; Grace will validate network and packaging notes for air‑gapped installs.

We should be able to deliver a complete package by 31 Mar. If anything looks like it requires an exception, we’ll call it out explicitly on each question in the survey.

Also, quick heads up on a couple of items we expect to flag as conditional:
- HSM integrations: we support standard PKCS11 HSMs but need an initial compatibility matrix (model/vendor) for deep validation.
- Air‑gapped automated updates: supported via a signed offline bundle + ops playbook; fully automatic OTA in air‑gap is not available.

We’ll upload docs to the Drive link and cc you when done. Can we tentatively schedule the 45m follow‑up for Tue 2 Apr 10:00–10:45 PT?

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@zephyrus.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Mar 2028 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: On‑Prem Capability Survey — Zephyrus (completed)

Alex / Team —

Attached are our completed survey responses and supporting artifacts. Highlights:

1) Installation and air‑gap
- Redwood Private v2.3.1 supports an offline installer (signed tarball) that installs the control plane and runtime.
- Recommended approach for air‑gapped PoC: provision a staging VLAN, apply signed bundles from an external jump host, validate node images via SHA256.
- We provide a step‑by‑step ops playbook and a checklist for security handover.

2) Key management
- Integrations: AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault (HSM SKS), and on‑prem PKCS#11 HSMs.
- We support envelope encryption where customer KMS holds root keys and Redwood holds ephemeral keys (customer retains key control).

3) SBOM and supply chain
- SBOM for redwood-private-v2.3.1 attached (CSV export). We also provide a signed SBOM manifest and recommended patch cadence (monthly patch windows with critical CVE hotfixes as needed).

4) Network and firewall requirements
- Minimal outbound egress for license token handshake (configurable to allow only via customer proxy) or fully air‑gapped offline activation. Ports and CIDR ranges are documented in the install plan.

5) Service assurance and rollback
- Canary rollout tool, per‑node health checks and automated circuit breakers. Rollback documented in the upgrade playbook.

Attached: redwood-private-v2.3.1-install-plan.pdf, SBOM_redwood-private_v2.3.1.csv

We flagged three survey items with conditional responses and notes (see section 9 of the PDF) — mainly around automated OTA in strict air‑gap, vendor‑specific HSM modules that require separate validation, and long‑term archive encryption key rotation workflows.

Uploading files now to the shared Drive (link below). Looking forward to the Tue 2 Apr call — the 10:00 PT slot works for us.

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/rfp/zephyrus/poa-2028-03

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Private Deployments | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-private-v2.3.1-install-plan.pdf (13 pages), SBOM_redwood-private_v2.3.1.csv (artifact)
From: J. Park <j.park@zephyrus.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Alex Kim <alex.kim@zephyrus.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 11:06:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: RFP: On‑Prem Capability Survey — Clarifications

Marissa / Rishi —

Thanks for the detailed package; a couple of quick clarifications before the call:

1) Offline activation: can you confirm the signed tarball activation requires a one‑time license handshake that can be done from a jump host in our DMZ? Are there any central Redwood endpoints polled post activation?

2) SBOM: can you provide a mapping of critical vs non‑critical components and an estimated CVE exposure window historically (we want to understand how fast critical fixes landed in production over the last 12 months).

3) KMS: during a live upgrade, how are keys rotated for persisted KV cache entries? Is there an automated rewrap operation or manual ops step?

4) Audit logs: can logs be forwarded to our SIEM (Splunk) in real time, and do you ship a structured schema?

If you can include short answers to the four bullets in the call prep, we’ll prioritize the items and keep the call to 30 minutes.

— J. Park
Head of Infrastructure Security | Zephyrus Systems

From: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: J. Park <j.park@zephyrus.com>, Alex Kim <alex.kim@zephyrus.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: On‑Prem Capability Survey — Clarifications & call prep

J. Park / Alex —

Thanks — responses below are short answers for the call prep; we’ll bring detailed technical notes to the meeting and can hand off follow up artifacts after.

1) Offline activation
- One‑time license handshake is supported from a customer DMZ jump host. After activation, Redwood does not require ongoing calls to public endpoints for runtime licensing when configured for fully offline mode. We do provide an optional telemetry endpoint in connected deployments; it’s off by default for air‑gapped installs.

2) SBOM / CVE remediation history
- Attached mapping: SBOM contains component criticality flags; historically our average Time‑to‑Fix for critical CVEs affecting production runtime has been 9 days (median) over the last 12 months; SLA exceptions for zero‑day fixes documented in the security runbook.

3) KMS / key rotation during upgrades
- We provide an automated rewrap utility that rotates root wrapping keys and rewraps persisted KV caches with minimal downtime (rolling rewrap strategy). For customers preferring manual ops, we provide a scripted playbook.

4) Audit logs to SIEM
- Yes: logs can be forwarded to Splunk/ELK via a syslog/HTTPS forwarder. We ship a JSON schema v1.4; sample mapping included in the install plan.

See you on the call.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Private
